beats.title: You have landed
body: Five of you, a boat, four logs and a week of food. A wooded coast, a lake, stone in the uplands, and nothing else at all — no roads, no shelter, and nobody coming: the boat’s whole company is named, and it has sailed.
You can raise a house. That is the only thing this settlement knows how to build. Everything else it will have to decide it wants.

beats.title: Something to work with
body: Hazel has made the first tools on this coast — a stone axe and a stone pick, out of two stones and a stick.
Bare hands took three times as long to fell a tree and would not open an ore seam at all. This is the point where the valley stops being survivable and starts being workable.

beats.title: Somebody was hired
body: Hazel could not get 4 wood and Odile could. Nobody ordered it and nobody volunteered — a price was named and taken.
It was taken on credit, which is what people pay each other with in a place that has not struck a coin. The debt is written down and it will be remembered.

beats.title: A roof
body: Hazel has raised the first house on this coast. Two beds, which means two people sleep indoors tonight.
It also means somebody else can come. Until now nobody would.

beats.title: A house somebody paid for
body: Odile has been sleeping on the ground and has stopped waiting for the settlement to agree that this is a problem. They have paid Ivo 4 wood out of their own pocket to put a house up, and the bed in it is theirs.
The people already housed had a fair objection — every house makes this more of a town and less of a coast. That objection is about the commons. This one is not being built out of the commons.

beats.title: Somebody bought a vote
body: Brant has nothing anybody wants and one thing they badly need, so they went to Odile beforehand with 2 wood out of their own pack and asked to be voted with.
Nobody wrote a rule allowing this. It is what a person with a stake and no power does, and whether it holds depends entirely on what sort of person took the goods.

beats.title: A trade
body: Liss and Odile have swapped 2 wood for 1 stone. Nobody minted anything, nobody agreed a price, and both of them are better off than they were.
This is what an economy is before there is any money in it. Everything else — coin, a rate, a market — is a convenience laid on top of two people seeing the sense in it.

beats.title: Nothing keeps in a sack
body: Hazel was carrying food and it went soft before they ate it. Until now a pack was the one place in this valley where nothing ever spoiled — better than the open store, better than a shed, better than anywhere a settlement could build.
It is the store’s job to keep things and the granary’s job to keep them longer. What is in your arms is only ever on its way somewhere.

beats.title: Somebody who is good at something
body: Ivo has made 13 things now and there is nobody on this coast better at forestry. It is not a title anybody gave them. It is the count.
A settlement where everybody is equally mediocre at everything has no reason to ask anybody in particular for anything. This one now has somebody to ask.

beats.title: Somebody changed trade
body: Ivo came ashore a builder and has spent long enough at something else that it is what they are: a forester, by the count of what they have actually done.
Nothing in this valley assigned them that and nothing can take it away. It is the same for every trade that has not been invented here yet — whoever ends up doing it will be the one who did it.

beats.title: They have decided the valley is big enough
body: A house was proposed and voted down, 1 to 4. Every house is two beds, and two beds is an invitation to somebody nobody here has met.
Not everyone came to a coast like this to live in a town. The motion can be put again, but not today.

beats.title: Somebody who is good at something
body: Hazel has made 13 things now and there is nobody on this coast better at farming. It is not a title anybody gave them. It is the count.
A settlement where everybody is equally mediocre at everything has no reason to ask anybody in particular for anything. This one now has somebody to ask.

beats.title: Somebody who is good at something
body: Odile has made 13 things now and there is nobody on this coast better at mining. It is not a title anybody gave them. It is the count.
A settlement where everybody is equally mediocre at everything has no reason to ask anybody in particular for anything. This one now has somebody to ask.

beats.title: Stacked outside
body: Liss carried a load to the stores, found no room in it, and put 3 of it on the ground beside the door. It is still there. It is just not under anything.

Nothing here holds anything by default — a boat holds twenty and a corner of somebody’s house holds twelve. Anybody hauling past will get that stack in on the day there is room for it, and the weather is working on it until somebody does.

beats.title: It does not keep
body: 6 food gathered in the landing has gone soft in the sack before anybody got to it. Nobody did anything wrong: berries in a bag on the ground are berries in a bag on the ground.
Somewhere dry to keep it is a building, and a building past a house is something this settlement has to vote for. Until then every hour spent gathering is an hour with a hole in it.

beats.title: The stack outside
body: the landing has been putting what will not fit on the ground beside the store, and the ground has started taking it. It is not gone the moment it is set down — anybody hauling past will get it back in the day there is room for it — but a heap on a wet coast is on a clock.
Somewhere to put things is a building, and a building past a house is something this settlement has to vote for.

beats.title: The first winter
body: The berries have stopped coming back and the wood is slow. What is in the stores is what there is until the thaw.
This is what the granary was for, and the shelter out at the workings, and every argument anybody had about laying something by. A settlement that voted those down finds out now.

beats.title: It takes things
body: Ivo was out past the settlement with a full pack when it turned, and came back with less than they set out to carry. Until now the weather here could make a day long and could make a roof rot, and it could not take anything out of anybody’s hands.

There are two answers to it and the settlement has to vote for either. Somewhere to put a load down out at the workings is one. Knowing at first light that it was going to turn is the other, and it is the one that gets the load home.

beats.title: The boat is gone
body: It was never going to last, and nobody could keep it — a hull hauled up a shingle beach and left to the weather.
Whatever this place turns out to be, it is home now.
